Specification of Communication Management
AUTOSAR AP R25-11
[SWS_CM_00197] Asynchronous behavior of method call with notification
Upstream requirements:
RS_CM_00213, RS_CM_00215, RS_AP_00114, RS_AP_00127, RS_-
AP_00138
⌈
To achieve asynchronous behavior of the method call with event-driven notification
on the result availability, the non-blocking method
then()
of
ara::core::Future
object shall be used. It allows to register a function, which gets asynchronously called
in case the future has a valid result.
⌋
Note:
In order to report an
ApApplicationError
(according to the interface descrip-
tion in the Manifest), the implementation of a service method stores the corresponding
ara::core::ErrorCode
representing this
ApApplicationError
(see [16]) into
the
ara::core::Promise
object, from which the
ara::core::Future
is returned
to the caller of the service method implementation. This
ara::core::ErrorCode
will then be used by the respective network binding to include the error information in
the method response message (see e.g., [SWS_CM_10308] and [SWS_CM_10428]
for the SOME/IP network binding or [SWS_CM_11102] and [SWS_CM_10431] for the
DDS network binding).
[SWS_CM_00822] Minimum Send Interval monitoring for for method calls by the
client
⌈
To protect receivers from flooding/overload, each method shall have a config-
urable Minimum Send Interval (see
ServiceInterfaceDeploymentElement
.
min-
imumSendInterval
), which specifies the minimum amount of time that shall pass
between two calls of the method by the client, i.e., the Minimum Send Interval limits the
maximum Tx frequency of a given method call in the network. If the application calls a
method by invoking the
operator()
of the respective method class,
ara::com
shall
check, whether the time since the last successful handover of the method call the un-
derlying transmission layer is greater than the specified Minimum Send Interval, i.e.,
